View A5 cells on an interactive map

a5_view.Rd

Renders A5 cells with deck.gl over a MapLibre basemap. Cells are drawn as filled pentagons; the viewer provides a basemap switcher, an opacity slider, a legend for numeric fills, hover tooltips, and an optional polygon-draw tool.

Usage

a5_view(
  cells,
  fill = "#74ac90ff",
  fill_identity = FALSE,
  palette = "Viridis",
  opacity = 0.3,
  tooltip = TRUE,
  elevation = NULL,
  elevation_scale = 1,
  border = "#74ac9080",
  border_width = 1,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  lng = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  zoom = NULL,
  globe = FALSE,
  basemap = c("dark", "light", "osm", "satellite"),
  draw_polygon = FALSE,
  aggregate = c("none", "rep_child", "mean"),
  lod_step = 1L
)

Arguments

cells

An a5R::a5_cell or a5R::a5_covering vector, or a data frame / tibble containing a column of either. A covering is drawn as the cells it stores, at their mixed resolutions; uncompact it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first to draw its cells at one resolution. Each row of a covering column is repeated once per stored cell. Pyramids (aggregate other than "none") need cells at one resolution.

fill

Fill colour specification. One of:

  • A single hex colour string (e.g. "#3388ff") for uniform fill.

  • A numeric vector (same length as cells) mapped to palette.

  • A character vector of hex colours (same length as cells) for per-cell colours.

  • An unquoted column name when cells is a data frame.

  • An expression evaluated against the columns of cells, in the style of ggplot2::aes(). This makes the colour helpers cells_rgb() and cells_pca_rgb() usable directly inside the call, e.g. a5_view(df, fill = cells_rgb(r, g, b)) or a5_view(df, fill = cells_pca_rgb(embedding)). The helpers tag their output so fill_identity is auto-enabled. Default: "#74ac90ff".

fill_identity

Logical. When TRUE, treat fill values as literal colours rather than mapping through palette. Accepts packed RGB integers ((R << 16) | (G << 8) | B) or hex colour strings. Auto-enabled when fill is produced by cells_rgb() / cells_pca_rgb() or any vector tagged with attr(x, "a5_identity") <- TRUE. Default: FALSE.

palette

Colour palette used when fill is numeric. Either a palette name accepted by grDevices::hcl.colors() (e.g. "viridis", "inferno", "plasma", "turbo", "rocket") or a character vector of hex colours (at least 2). Default: "Viridis".

opacity

Numeric scalar, initial layer opacity (0–1). An interactive slider is provided in the viewer to adjust at runtime. Default: 0.3.

tooltip

Logical, or a character vector of column names from cells. TRUE (default) shows the hovered cell's id plus its fill value when fill is a numeric mapping. A character vector adds those columns to the tooltip (requires aggregate = "none"). FALSE disables the tooltip. The tooltip only appears over cells present in the data (see the section on hover and click below).

elevation

Column name for 3D extrusion, or NULL for flat.

elevation_scale

Numeric scalar, scale factor for elevation.

border

Border (stroke) colour for cell outlines, or NULL for no borders. A single colour string (e.g. "#ffffff", "white"). Default: "#74ac9080".

border_width

Numeric scalar, border width in pixels. Default: 1.

width, height

Widget dimensions. Default: NULL (fills container).

lng, lat, zoom

Initial map view. If NULL (default), auto-centres on the cell centroids.

globe

Logical. Use MapLibre's globe projection instead of the default Mercator map. Default: FALSE.

basemap

Character vector of basemap styles to make available. Options are "dark", "light" and "osm" (OpenFreeMap vector tiles; no API key), "satellite" (Esri World Imagery) and "none". The first element is shown initially. When more than one is given, an interactive selector is shown. Default: c("dark", "light", "osm", "satellite").

draw_polygon

Logical. When TRUE, adds a "Draw polygon" toggle to the controls panel. While draw mode is active, clicks place polygon vertices and a double-click closes the polygon. On completion, the polygon is emitted to Shiny as a WKT string at input$<id>_polygon_draw; the drawn outline is held on screen until the user toggles draw mode off, presses Escape, or starts a new polygon. While draw mode is on, double-click-to-zoom is suppressed and cell-pick click events do not fire. The widget itself does not visualise which cells fall inside the polygon: resolve the WKT server-side (e.g. with a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells()) and update the map fills via a5_view_update(). The outline is drawn with straight edges on the Web Mercator map, but a5R::a5_polygon_to_cells() reads edges as great circles, so along a long edge the selected cells can stray from the outline; place more vertices to keep them close. Only useful in a Shiny context. Default: FALSE.

aggregate

How parent cells are summarised when zooming out. One of:

  • "none" (default): no precomputed pyramid. All cells are shipped as Arrow IPC and rendered through deck.gl's A5Layer. Cheapest to build, suitable for small to medium datasets.

  • "rep_child": each parent inherits the row of the child whose payload (RGBA + optional fill_value/elevation) is closest in Euclidean distance to its parent's mean. Preserves real values, no blending. Use for embedding/RGB visualisations.

  • "mean": each numeric payload column is averaged independently within the parent group. Best for scalar fields; blends colours in RGB space, which can mute embedding visualisations. When set to "rep_child" or "mean", the pyramid is serialised to parquet with a spatial row-group index. The browser decodes only the row groups intersecting the viewport at the level of detail matching the current zoom. Inside Shiny the parquet file is served over HTTP with byte-range support, so only the footer and the visible row groups are ever transferred; elsewhere it is embedded in the widget as base64.

lod_step

Integer >= 1, gap between successive precomputed LODs (only used when aggregate != "none"). 1 (default) precomputes every level from the data resolution down to the floor (LOD 2); larger values trade size for fewer levels and more visible popping at zoom transitions.

Value

An htmlwidget.

Hover, click and Shiny inputs

Hover and click only resolve to cells that are present in the data: the tooltip, the outline highlight and the Shiny inputs below stay empty over parts of the map with no cell. With aggregate = "none" the resolved cell is the leaf cell under the cursor. With a pyramid it is the cell at the level of detail currently on screen, so the id and value reported are those of the pentagon you can see; zoom in to reach the leaf cells.

When rendered in Shiny with output id <id>, the widget sets:

  • input$<id>_hover: hex id of the cell under the cursor (or NULL).

  • input$<id>_click: hex id of the clicked cell; clicking it again, or clicking empty map, clears it.

  • input$<id>_cursor, input$<id>_click_coord: list(lng, lat) of the pointer.

  • input$<id>_polygon_draw: WKT of a completed polygon (see draw_polygon).
